main_text.p: 1. PORRO, Illustrissimi & Potentissimi Domini, ut uberius cognoscatur virulentissimus, malitiosissimus & rabiosissimus animus horum hominum erga Reformatos cujuscunque dignitatis, status, conditionis sint; attendendum est ad horrendam maledicentiam, inauditam petulantiam insolentissi-ma convitia ac nullo modo tolerandas contumelias quibus in vindiciis suis utuntur contra Reformatos Reges, principes, Magistratus, Doctores & Pastores Ecclesiarum, vivos & mortuos, contra populos omnes Reformatos, imo contra omne[?] Reges principes Magistratus aliosque qui cum Arminianis non sentiunt de tolerantia omnis generis Hæreticorum, præcipuè Antitrinitariorum. Nam Maledicentiam quâ me quidem petiere in vindiciis suis facile contemno: cui triste foret & molestum à bonis[?] viris & piis opprobrio affici. Sed ab his hominibus qui summorum, ut ostendi & porrò ostendam, scelerum rei sunt, hoc est ab Antitrinitariis & qui Reformatos omnes cujus un[?]que digni-tatis & conditionis sunt opprimere moliuntur, ab iis, inquam, contumelia affici & indigna pati gloriosum coram DEO, & boni viri indicium est coram hominibus. Maledicentia & petulantia Antitrinitariis Hæreticis inde ab initio consueta fuit. Arius Orthodoxos Doctores & populos convitiis etiam petulantissimè proscinde-

page.notes: Printed page number "55" at top right. Running head "LIB. I. CAP. VIII." is printed at top left. Large initial "P" is joined to "ORRO" as "PORRO". Catchword "profcinde-" is printed at right below the last full line, with its hyphen. The word "cujus un-que" is blurred at the line end, so "un" is uncertain. "omne" is followed by a faint mark that may be a colon or a letter, marked [?]. "bon's" in the line "a bon's viris" is read as "bonis" but is doubtful. The first printed line "corporali ratione." begins a summary whose earlier items are on the previous page. Long s is normalised, and the "ff" ligature in "insolentiffima" and "petulantiffime" is read as "ss". Spacing from the printed typesetting has been normalised.
